en.title: Godzilla Minus Zero Team Reveals Dream Kaiju for Hypothetical Sequel
en.summary: While Godzilla Minus Zero is currently dominating screens, the creative minds behind the film are already dreaming of future monster mashups. The team behind Takashi Yamazaki's latest kaiju epic has shared which classic monsters they'd love to see return.
en.body:
The roar of **Godzilla Minus Zero** has barely faded, and already, the minds behind this critically acclaimed film are looking to the future. Director **Takashi Yamazaki**’s latest entry in the Minus Goji Universe, which pits Godzilla against the legendary **King Ghidorah**, has captivated audiences worldwide. While the possibility of a third film in this iteration remains unconfirmed, the creative team has enthusiastically shared their personal wish lists for future kaiju encounters.

During recent discussions, key members of the **Godzilla Minus Zero** production offered intriguing insights into their dream collaborations. **Takayuki Ueki**, the Visual Effects Supervisor, expressed a desire to see the formidable **Biollante** return. This plant-based behemoth, known for its serpentine tendrils and cellular regeneration, last appeared in **Godzilla vs. Biollante** (1989) and presents a unique biological horror that would offer a stark contrast to the mechanical might of Ghidorah. Meanwhile, VFX Artist **Tatsuji Nojima** championed the return of **Rodan**, the volcanic pteranodon-like creature that has been a fan favorite since its debut in 1956's **Rodan**. Rodan, often depicted as a force of nature born from nuclear anxieties, has a rich history in the Toho canon, appearing in six previous films and offering aerial combat possibilities that could redefine spectacle.

Perhaps the most anticipated dream inclusion comes from Producer **Kazuaki Kishida**, who named **Destoroyah** as his preferred monster. This ultimate destroyer, a product of the Oxygen Destroyer's residual energy, is a terrifyingly powerful adversary that famously battled Godzilla in **Godzilla vs. Destoroyah** (1995). Kishida, however, was quick to temper excitement, emphasizing that these are purely speculative desires and no concrete plans for a third film are in place. Nevertheless, the mere mention of these iconic kaiju ignites the imagination of fans who crave the next grand clash of titans.

## The Allure of the Classics

The choices made by the **Godzilla Minus Zero** team highlight a deep appreciation for the legacy of Toho's kaiju cinema. **Rodan**, for instance, is more than just a flying monster; its original conception served as a potent commentary on the burgeoning nuclear threat of the post-war era. Bringing back creatures like **Biollante**, **Rodan**, and **Destoroyah** isn't just about nostalgia; it's about reintroducing complex, thematically rich monsters that can offer fresh narrative and visual possibilities. These creatures represent different facets of humanity's relationship with nature, technology, and destruction, providing fertile ground for Yamazaki's thoughtful approach to the genre.

## What's Next

Fans eager to see **Godzilla Minus Zero** continue its cinematic reign can catch it in North America on November 6th, 2026, following its Japan release on November 3rd, 2026. While the future of the franchise beyond this installment is still under wraps, the creative sparks flying from the **Godzilla Minus Zero** team suggest that the world of Godzilla is far from finished evolving.

And while there is no guarantee that Yamazaki and crew will make another Godzilla movie, the team did recently discuss which giant monsters they would love to see in a hypothetical third movie. Here were their responses: Takayuki Ueki (Visual Effects Supervisor) – Biollante Tatsuji Nojima (VFX Artist) – Rodan Kazuaki Kishida (Producer) – Destoroyah Now, Kishida was quick to remind everyone that there is currently no third Godzilla movie in production and there have been no formal discussions about any of the creative plans for that hypothetical movie. BUT, for the purposes of fun, let’s look at each of those three kaiju in case you don’t happen to be familiar with their work. Rodan is probably the biggest name in that group. Featured in six previous films, the flying creature that is modeled after a Pteranodon is widely considered to be one of the great monsters in Japanese cinema. Rodan was conceived as a kind of commentary on the growing nuclear threat of the Soviet Union. Interestingly, Rodan has historically functioned as an ally/rival to Godzilla, so featuring the creature in a future movie wouldn’t only offer some name value but would potentially open the door to some more complex kaiju relationship dynamics (it’s always complicated with kaiju, isn’t it?). Biollante is an interesting pull, but hardly a surprise when you think of how much fun the VFX team could have bringing that creature to life. The plant-hybrid monster hasn’t been featured in nearly as many films as some of the more iconic kaiju, but one look at the creature’s design is all you really need to know how incredible it would be to see this thing brought to life by an exceptional modern VFX team. Of the three options above, that would also be my personal favorite. That said, Destoroyah is a fascinating option.
